absent: Definition and derivation of access masks and shifts from descriptors.
Behavior of guest ownership marking for debug state.
Layout of vcpu system register storage and slot numbering.
Full behavior of monitor helpers for counters, events, masks and control.
Timer helpers for instance lookup, offset handling and physical time reads.
Semantics of visibility codes and table search and matching.
Behavior of undefined, read-only and write-only fault helpers.
Tail of userspace timer count read and safe feature value helper beyond truncation.
Lock ordering and other users of VM configuration state.
Host feature predicates for monitor, pointer authentication and thirty two bit support.

findings.text: Guest accesses to breakpoint and watchpoint value and control registers trap into a handler that resolves the encoding to per-vcpu debug storage, applies a masked read or write of the requested field, marks debug state as guest owned, and reports success; unresolvable encodings report failure.

Debug register demultiplexing selects among four per-vcpu arrays using the encoding class field with the encoding row field as index; two class values map to breakpoint values while three other distinct values map respectively to breakpoint controls, watchpoint values and watchpoint controls, and any other class is a fatal configuration error returning no storage.

Partial debug register accesses share a descriptor-derived mask and shift; writes preserve unselected bits of the stored word while inserting the supplied field, and reads extract the selected field right aligned.

Userspace views of debug registers operate on the whole stored word without masking, returning an invalid argument error when no storage exists; reset writes the descriptor default into storage and returns it, returning zero when storage is missing.

Reset of memory attribute and implementation control registers copies the current host hardware value into the vcpu store, while reset of the multiprocessor affinity register uses a vcpu-id-derived computed value; each returns the installed value.
Multiprocessor affinity value packs the numeric vcpu identifier into three affinity levels with four bits in level zero, eight bits each in levels one and two, and always sets bit thirty one.

Register visibility can force hiding unconditionally, expose performance monitor registers only when the vcpu has a monitor, and expose pointer authentication key registers only when the vcpu has that feature.

Performance monitor resets start from a poisoned word then narrow it to implemented state: generic registers keep only implemented counter bits plus cycle bit, event counters keep low thirty two bits, event types keep the hardware event mask when a monitor exists, selector keeps its selector field, and control starts cleared except for a long-cycle flag when thirty two bit EL0 is unavailable.
Unknown register reset installs poison value 0x1de7ec7edbadc0de into the vcpu store for the descriptor slot.

User level monitor access is granted when the enable gate in the user enable register matches the operation class or when the vcpu runs privileged; otherwise an undefined exception is injected and the access fails. Distinct gates cover general access, software increment, cycle counter and event counter classes.

Guest control register access first applies the general user gate. Writes update only writable control bits through the monitor handler while preserving other bits and forcing long-cycle when needed; reads return the monitor view with profiling and cycle-reset bits forced to zero.

Guest selector access uses the event-counter gate, storing the full supplied word but returning only the selector field. Guest common-event identification access is read only, uses the general gate, and returns the monitor-provided identification word filtered by descriptor mask and shift with parity selected by encoding.

Counter index validation compares the requested index against the count field of the control register, allowing the dedicated cycle index regardless of count; out of range event indexes inject an undefined exception and fail the access.

Guest event and cycle counter accesses decode the architectural encoding to a counter index, apply the matching user gate, validate the index, then delegate to monitor value helpers; writes need the additional general gate. Direct encodings derive index from row and class fields, selected-counter encoding uses the current selector, cycle encodings use the dedicated cycle index.

Guest event-type access uses the general gate and validates the index. Selected-type encoding resolves the index through the current selector, direct encodings derive it from row and class fields with the cycle position aliased to the cycle filter register; writes update the monitor event type and restore guest monitor state while reads return the stored word.

Enable, interrupt-enable and overflow status registers share one stored word per class with set and clear views distinguished by an encoding bit; userspace and guest writes are masked to accessible counters, set views OR bits while clear views AND-complement bits, and enable changes trigger monitor reprogramming while generic class updates request a monitor reload.

Guest reads of the monitor information register are read only and expose only the slots field taken from per-VM stored slots; writes take a read-only fault path. Userspace reads return the same slots view.

Userspace updates to the slots field serialize on the VM configuration lock, reject any bits outside slots, enforce immutability once the VM has run, and otherwise accept zero to restore legacy behavior while rejecting non-zero values that differ from current state.

Software increment is write only, uses its dedicated user gate, masks to accessible counters and delegates to the monitor increment helper. User-enable register writes require privileged mode and store only the defined enable mask, while reads return the masked stored value.

Userspace control updates serialize on the VM configuration lock when adjusting the VM-wide counter count, applying only before first run, without nesting, without strict monitor mode, and within hardware limits; the stored word is then narrowed to the writable mask with long-cycle forced when needed and a monitor reload is requested.

Descriptor tables for debug registers bind trap, reset and userspace handlers per breakpoint and watchpoint index; monitor tables bind reset, visibility and per-register access with assigned slots; activity monitor tables force undefined handling; pointer authentication tables bind undefined handling with feature-gated visibility.

Per-vcpu debug state provides four indexed arrays for breakpoint values, breakpoint controls, watchpoint values and watchpoint controls, each addressed by the encoding row field after class demultiplexing.

Register descriptors observed here carry encoding fields for class, row and column, a vcpu slot identifier, a reset default and handler hooks; encodings select storage or monitor index while slot identifiers select the vcpu stored word.

Timer trap handling maps each trapped encoding to an internal timer instance and register kind covering value, control, compare and count views, redirects EL0 physical and virtual views to hyp timers when in hyp context with E2H set, routes count views by hyp context, and delegates to timer read or write helpers with unknown encodings taking an undefined path.

Userspace timer control writes clear the latched status bit before storing, while userspace count writes install a counter offset derived from physical time and supplied value unless a VM-wide offset flag is set; count reads return physical time minus the stored offset.
Failure to resolve debug storage marks the VM as buggy and yields no storage; the trap path then fails and the reset path returns zero, with the buggy mark preventing the VM from ever running.

Invalid descriptor slot use, direct event-type decoding errors, and write attempts to read-only identification registers trigger bug checks; an undecoded counter access warns; these indicate host programming errors rather than guest recoverable faults.
Two small header helpers are shared within the dossier: one derives the affinity value from the vcpu identifier and one installs the poison default for unknown registers with slot range checks.
